context:
Treat this as repository-shape work, not corpus work. The slim-down
is the load-bearing step; the mirror is mechanical once the target
shape is clear. Expect this to need explicit user approval at W2
(force-push to a shared branch) and W4 (CI workflow change).
description:
The design intent for `published-results` is that it contains **only**
the results corpus and the metadata the results explorer needs (bundle
JSONs, per-bundle manifests, `corpus-inventory.json`, the small set of
human-readable corpus docs like `README.md` / `CORPUS_NOTES.md` /
`SEED_CORPUS_SPEC.md`, and the corpus depth validator
`validate_corpus.py`).

Reality on 2026-05-03 is different on two axes:

1. **`published-results` is fat, not slim.** It currently sits at the
   May-1 snapshot of develop (SHA `520d7055d`, 13,809 tracked files
   including the full `benchbox/`, `tests/`, `_project/`, `_binaries/`,
   all `.github/workflows/`, etc.). Develop has 1674 commits since.
2. **The explorer build does not actually consume `published-results`.**
   `docs.yml` and `results-explorer-browser.yml` trigger only on
   `main` (push and PR). There is no promote-from-published-results
   workflow. Bundles merged to `published-results` therefore do not
   reach the explorer's static build pipeline; the explorer renders
   `results-data/` from develop → main.

Consequence: the Phase 2 contributor flow described in
`docs/operations/results-phase-2-runbook.md` is convention-only at
present — landing a corpus PR on `published-results` does not move
bundles to where the explorer reads. The
`results-explorer-uat-corpus-integrate-validated-bundles` TODO had
to land its 188 community-submission bundles via develop for the
explorer to render them, which deviates from the runbook.

This TODO does the structural cleanup: slim `published-results` down
to the intended corpus-only shape, mirror the UAT-20260502 188-bundle
delta onto it so the conventional contributor target is current, and
decide whether the explorer build should also fire on
`published-results` (or whether a develop ↔ published-results sync
workflow is the right answer).

anti_patterns.dont: couple this to the byte-stable bundle emission TODO
anti_patterns.instead: this TODO just moves bytes; the canonicalization TODO changes how bytes are written.
anti_patterns.why: they are separable concerns and bundling them grows scope

anti_patterns.dont: create a develop -> published-results sync that also overwrites contributor PRs in flight
anti_patterns.instead: the sync should rebase or merge, never force-push over contributor branches.

anti_patterns.dont: slim published-results without explicit user authorization for the force-push
anti_patterns.instead: gate on user approval at W2.
anti_patterns.why: it is a shared branch with PRs that may be in flight or with stale-but-still-referenced commits

deferrals.reason: The slim-down resets published-results to a single commit; restoring per-PR history would require replaying every Phase 2 PR ever merged, which is not the deliverable here.
deferrals.resolved_reason: [G4 sweep] non-actionable: Reason explicitly states backfilling git history with curated messages is not the deliverable for the slim-down; deliberately excluded scope.
deferrals.summary: Backfilling published-results' git history with curated commit messages

preserves.behavior: All bundles currently checked-in on develop's results-data/bundles/ remain merge-able through whichever new flow lands.
The per-bundle manifest hash contract is intact across the slim-down (bundle bytes are not edited; only branch shape changes).
The runbook (`docs/operations/results-phase-2-runbook.md`) reflects the new flow before declaring W4 done.

scope_rules.path_glob: docs/development/adr/ (if a new ADR is needed)
published-results branch contents (via separate branch & PR)

verifications.description: published-results' file count matches the slim-corpus-only target.
verifications.expected: Approximately the count from the W1 ADR (target: hundreds, not 13k+).

verifications.description: Explorer build picks up new bundles from the chosen flow (W4 verification).
verifications.expected: A test merge to published-results either triggers explorer rebuild OR a documented separate develop PR is opened.

work_units.notes:
Land a short ADR (or extend `docs/operations/results-phase-2-runbook.md`)
listing the exact paths that may live on `published-results`:
`results-data/` (full subtree), `.gitignore`, `LICENSE`,
`CONTRIBUTING.md`, optionally `README.md` (with corpus-flow guidance,
not the develop README), and minimal CI to run the per-bundle
validators. Everything else gets removed when published-results is
slimmed. Confirm with the user before doing the slim-down.
work_units.summary: Decide the canonical published-results contents and confirm with maintainers

work_units.notes:
Fresh-orphan-branch approach: build a new commit on top of the
decided subtree, then force-push (with explicit user authorization)
`published-results` to that commit. This loses the May-1 develop
history on `published-results` but the history is preserved on
develop and main; published-results' own log only ever needs to
describe the corpus changes that have landed on it. Document the
one-time slim-down in the same ADR/runbook.
work_units.summary: Slim published-results down to the intended subtree

work_units.notes:
Fork off the slimmed `published-results`, copy the bundle JSONs +
per-bundle manifests + regenerated `corpus-inventory.json` from the
develop-side staging (results-data/bundles/* on develop after the
parent TODO merged), open a draft PR vs `published-results`. The PR
diff should be ~376 file additions (188 bundles + 188 manifests) +
inventory regen + a small README update — small and review-friendly.
Target trust labels, validator outputs, and cohort gate behavior
must match what landed on develop.
work_units.summary: Mirror the UAT-20260502 188-bundle integration onto slim published-results

work_units.notes:
Pick one of:
  a) A scheduled workflow that opens a draft PR mirroring the
     `results-data/` subtree from develop to published-results when
     drift is detected.
  b) Extend `docs.yml` / `results-explorer-browser.yml` triggers to
     also fire on `published-results` push events, so a merge to
     that branch directly feeds the explorer build.
  c) Document explicitly that `published-results` is convention-only
     (Phase 2 contributor target) and that develop is the real
     source of truth — and accept that "PR vs published-results"
     must be paired with a develop merge.
Whichever option lands, capture the decision in the runbook so
future contributor PRs and maintainer reviews are not surprised.
